Unit positions come from the Revolutionary War workbook (the Cowpens rows), built from Morgan's report, Tarleton's and Howard's accounts, the journals and memoirs of men in the ranks, the Army's 1996 staff ride handbook, the Army War College study of 1928 and the National Park Service's handbook and waysides. Nothing here has been checked by a historian.

No map made at the time shows this ground, and the accounts give distances, not places. Every unit is therefore placed by distance along the Green River Road, which still crosses the field, counted from the spot where Tarleton's column came out of the woods. Lines may be 50 to 100 m from where they really stood; none is rated better than medium.

The clock follows the staff ride's maps: first shots about 07:00, the end about 07:50. Eyewitnesses say only "about sunrise", which was at 07:07; one Army study puts everything an hour later. Tap a unit to see the range of times its record allows.
Solid symbols are positions a source gives. Dashed symbols are worked out or are the last position on record. A question mark means the place is doubtful.
Symbols are blue for the Americans and red for the British and Loyalist troops. Zoom in to see Pickens's line by its regiments and Howard's by its parts.

The current map is the US Geological Survey's topographic map, and Satellite its aerial photography, both streamed from the USGS. If they cannot be reached, a simplified drawing of OpenStreetMap roads and streams is shown instead.

Where the sources disagree (the hour, the numbers, which riflemen were on the right, how far Howard fell back, who brought the militia back), the workbook's Hypotheses sheet gives each reading and says which one the playback follows.

Unit positions come from the Revolutionary War workbook (the Guilford Courthouse rows), built from Cornwallis's and Greene's reports, Lee's and Tarleton's accounts, journals of men in the ranks, the National Park Service's study and troop movement plans of 1971 (Charles Hatch) and the Marine Corps University Press staff ride of 2021. Nothing here has been checked by a historian.

On the battlefield every unit is read from Hatch's five plans, laid on today's ground by the park boundary. Lines may be 75 m from where he drew them, and he drew them from accounts that give the order of the lines and rough distances, not places on the ground: so every position is rated low and carries a question mark.

The clock follows the staff ride: the British advance about 13:00, the first line breaks about 13:15, the third line is fought from 14:45 and the Continentals leave about 15:30. Cornwallis put the start at half past one, Greene about noon. The morning fights near New Garden are placed at three road junctions and may be an hour or two out. Tap a unit to see the range of times its record allows.
Solid symbols are positions a source gives. Dashed symbols are worked out or are the last position on record. A question mark means the place is doubtful.

Symbols are blue for the Americans and red for the British, German and Loyalist troops. The brigades of regulars are shown by their regiments throughout. Militia brigades that broke are taken off the map a few minutes after they leave their line, and the Continentals are shown as one column once they retreat.

The playback opens on "1781 with terrain", a reconstruction: the road, creeks, fences and houses as Hatch drew them in 1971, on today's ground, and west of his sheet the road of the 1951 survey. The map details (the i button) list each line with its source and how sure it is, and offer Hatch's own plans, phase by phase. The current map is the US Geological Survey's topographic map and Satellite its aerial photography, both streamed from the USGS.

Where the sources disagree (the hours, which militia brigade stood north of the road, where the third line stood, how many guns the British had, whether Cornwallis fired on his own Guards), the workbook's Hypotheses sheet gives each reading and says which one the playback follows.

Two places named in the day lie off the map and are shown at its edge with an arrow and their distance: Deep River Friends Meeting House, where Cornwallis camped the night before, and the iron works on Troublesome Creek, where Greene's army halted that night.
